alerts.headline: High Surf Advisory issued September 28 at 3:00PM HST until September 29 at 6:00AM HST by NWS Honolulu HI
alerts.description:
...HIGH SURF ADVISORY FOR SOUTH FACING SHORES OF KAUAI AND NIIHAU
NOW IN EFFECT THROUGH 6 AM TUESDAY...

...HIGH SURF ADVISORY FOR OAHU MOLOKAI LANAI MAUI AND THE BIG
ISLAND IS CANCELLED...

.Short to medium period south-southwest swell from Hurricane Nolo
is generating advisory level surf for south facing shores of
Kauai and Niihau. This swell is expected to diminish slightly
during the next 24 hours but uncertainty remains with how quickly
this will occur.

* WHAT...Large surf of 7 to 10 feet.

* WHERE...South facing shores of Kauai and Niihau.

* WHEN...Until 6 AM HST Tuesday.

* IMPACTS...Moderate. Strong breaking waves and strong currents
will make swimming dangerous.
alerts.instruction:
Heed all advice from ocean safety officials. When in doubt, don't
go out.

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS Central Pacific Hurricane Center Honolulu HI
Issued by NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
200 AM HST Tue Sep 29 2026

For the central North Pacific...between 140W and 180W:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Hurricane
Polo, near the Baja California Peninsula of Mexico, on Hurricane
Nolo, located several hundred miles west of Honolulu, Hawaii, and on
Tropical Storm Rachel, located few hundred miles south-southwest of
Lazaro Cardenas, Mexico.

Well East-Southeast of the Hawaiian Islands (EP91):
An area of low pressure located well east-southeast of the Hawaiian
Islands is producing limited showers and thunderstorms this morning.
Only a slight increase in shower and thunderstorm organization is
needed for it to become a tropical depression during the next day or
two while it moves slowly east-northeastward. Environmental
conditions are expected to become less conducive for development
late this week.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...high...90 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...high...90 percent.

$$
Forecaster Kelly

aiBriefing: Na dziś (29 września) sytuacja jest umiarkowanie podwyższona, ale wasza podróż zaczyna się dopiero za 2 dni, czyli 2 października. Obecny alert wysokiej fali (High Surf Advisory) dotyczy tylko Kauai i Niihau i wygasa dziś rano — nie obejmuje Oahu, Big Island ani Maui, czyli wysp z waszej trasy, i i tak skończy się zanim wystartujecie. Huragan Nolo (kategoria 3) znajduje się około 652 km od trasy, ale jest to aktywne zjawisko krótkoterminowe, więc powinno się oddalić lub osłabić przed waszym przylotem. CPHC wskazuje też na 90% szans na uformowanie się nowego systemu w ciągu 7 dni daleko na wschód-południowy wschód od Hawajów, poruszającego się w stronę wschodnio-północno-wschodnią, czyli oddalającego się od wysp — warto to jednak monitorować bliżej daty wylotu, bo prognozy mogą się zmienić. Na razie nic nie wskazuje na bezpośrednie zagrożenie dla waszej podróży.
